EventName: Throat Punch Thursday - Summer MTB Short Track (XCC) Race Series
EventNotes:
Throat Punch Thursday 

MTB Short Track (XCC) Training Races
Summer Series
 


Powered by RVA Racing | USAC Sanctioned | National Points Qualifier

EVENT IS RAIN OR SHINE!


Race Nights

August 13 • August 20 • August 27
Heats start at 6:00 PM sharp. Know your category start time. Don’t roll up late unless you like watching from the sidelines.

Dogwood Dell - Barker Field: 1300 Blanton Ave, Richmond, VA 23221 (Google Maps)


The Rules - Pay Attention.

  • MTBs only!
  • This is USA Cycling Sanctioned MTB Race - USAC XCC format and rules apply.
  • Keep your Bib Plate. Bib plates are issued for the series.
  • Check in. Starts at 5:30. ALL racers MUST check in before each race – each day.
  • Registration closes at NOON on race day
  • NO WALK-ON REGISTRATIONS  


START TIMES

  • 6:00 PM - Fight Club
    • Intermediate Men & Boys (7-laps)
    • Beginner Men & Boys (5-laps)
    • Beginner Women & Girls (5-laps)     
  • 6:30 PM – Bareknuckle Brawlers
    • Expert Men & Boys (9-laps)
    • Masters Men & Women (7-laps)
    • Expert Women & Girls (9-laps)
    • Intermediate Women & Girls (7-laps)
  • 7:00 PM - The THROAT PUNCH
    • Rolling Start. 2-laps. All Out. No Hiding.
    • Open Men & Women / Boys & Girls (2-laps)


Race Format:

  • The TPT races are held on a course of .50 - .65 miles in lap distance with 60 - 75 feet of elevation gain each lap.
  • Lap counts are estimated based on first lap time.
  • Podiums based on most laps, lowest time.
  • Riders will cover around 4-10 laps during the 17-22-minute duration of their heat.
  • USAC points are scored for EACH race. 


The Course.

  • We are NOT racing on the Dogwood trails.
  • Each week's course is a custom, hand-built track right by the pavilion next to Barker Field.
  • This course is VERY spectator friendly - bring the crew and your best heckle game.
  • And yes - it changes every week to keep it spicy. Stay sharp.


Course Drops.

  • We design each course the week of the race.
  • Registered racers will receive course drops via email.


The Vibe:

Expect elbows-out racing. Bring your lungs, bring your legs, and maybe bring an ice pack for that ego (short track has a way of finding you).

It’s fast. It’s ridiculous. It’s fun.
  

USAC Sanctioning and Points:

  • ONLY USAC annual license holders will receive points!
  • Annual license holders ranked in order of finish for reporting.
  • Forget to enter your USAC ID at registration = NO POINTS.
  • ALL 3 races are USAC XCC qualifying opportunities for Nationals.
  • ALL 3 races allow you to earn USAC points for XCC Nationals.


Timing.

The TPT is electronically timed. Your bib plate is your RFID timing chip and should be mounted securely to your bars (top of plate) and the bottom of the plate should be mounted to cables, or in a way that makes the number clearly visible from the front of the bike. 

If you bend the plate, try to make it aero, don’t have it secured properly, or alter it in any way, we will NOT get a read. And that will mean all your hard work was for nuthin’ – so please don’t. Come find us if you have any questions on race day. Well also be checking on you.


Other.

Volunteers - We REALLY need volunteers to make this event happen and start on time.

  • 5:00 PM (or sooner): we start marking the course
  • 7:45 PM: course teardown
  • Please email dennis@rvaracing.com if you can help or show up on race day.


RVA Racing brings you bike racing, built by bike racers - We're grassroots, but professionally savage.

EventNotes:
Welcome to the 2026 Great Finger Lakes Bike Tour! We are opening registration early to allow riders to secure their spots while we finalize the finer details of the weekend.

 

From the rolling vineyards of the wine country to the historic paths that shaped a nation, this isn’t just a bike ride—it’s a fellowship on wheels.

 

What’s Waiting for You?

  • The Grand Finale Dinner: Celebrate your miles at our exclusive catered dinner hosted at our beautiful lakeside pavilion. Toast to new friends as the sun sets over the lake.

STBC Membership Requirement

This event is hosted exclusively for Southern Tier Bicycle Club members.

  • Not a member yet? For just 15 dollars a year, you gain access to this event and our full calendar of club activities.
  • Join the Club Here — Membership must be active to participate. Not sure if you are already a member? Email bike@southerntierbicycleclub.org to inquire about your membership status.

 

Event Swag & Merchandise Store

Commemorate your ride with our limited release 2026 Great Finger Lakes Bike Tour t-shirt and other event gear.

Important: The Merchandise Store is hosted on a separate platform and may close earlier than event registration to allow for production time. Order early to ensure you don't miss out!

  • Separate Transaction: Gear must be purchased via the Online Store. Store Closes Sunday, July 19at 11:59 PM
  • Delivery Options: Choose flat-rate shipping to your home or select "Pickup at Worldwide Print" and we will distribute at the event.
  • Support the Club: Our store also features a Donation Option. Your contributions directly support STBC’s mission to promote cycling opportunities in our community. We appreciate your generosity!

 

The Rides (Tentative)

You can view the routes here: Planned Rides

SAG support is provided on Saturday rides only.

Meals & Refreshments

  • Pre-Ride: Fresh coffee and snacks available at the start.
  • Post-Ride: A traditional BBQ dinner and our signature event cake.

 

Registration Details

  • Closing Date: Registration remains open until sold out or until one week prior to the event.
  • Note: We do not offer "ride-only" registrations; this is an all-inclusive event.

 

Accommodations

If you are looking to stay over at Cayuga Lake State Park, be sure to make reservations through the Reserve America website.

Welcome to Something New!

The Sawtooth Stage Race is the Midwest's only multi-day mountain bike trail race! The Superior Cycling Association is excited to partner with COGGS to bring this inaugural event to the North Shore. Race it gun to tape as a classic XC course, or sit back and rip the Gravity Segments like an enduro. Either way, take in every mile of the SCA's trail network, make new friends, and embrace the challenge of something new! The Sawtooth Stage Race offers every rider a new way to test their endurance, skill, and strategy over three days of epic singletrack racing!

The Race Within the Race

A stage race is a format that forces a rider to choose when to spend energy and when to save it. Legs, race tactics, and recovery all have a part to play here. A match burned on Friday is one less in the box for Sunday. The Sawtooth Stage Race gives racers the chance to compete for awards in three categories, but there is so much more than just awards to play for here.

The Stage Win is like any other cross country mountain bike race, the win goes to the rider with the fastest course time on the day (chip time in the ITT, gun time in the head to head stages).

The General Classification the "GC", is like the yellow jersey in the Tour, or the Maglia Rosa in the Giro. The rider with the shortest cumulative time over all three full courses stands on the top step.

The Gravity Classification tests technical skill through 9 independently timed segments. The rider with the shortest cumulative time over the segments wins this classification. (The gravity segments are built into each course, so it is possible for a racer to compete in both categories. See maps below for details.)

The Stages

 

Friday August 21, 4pm-7pm: ITT Prologue: 4.6mi, 350ft-  The tone for the weekend will be set with a short rip around the Britton Peak trails. This will be an individual time trial with riders allowed to start any time between 4pm and 7pm. There will be one Gravity segment on this course on Skookum. (Skookum is a black trail, be ready for some minor drops. Some riders may want to pre-ride this one.) Plate pickup and race information will be at the trailhead. Stage awards will be done as call ups the following morning.

 

Saturday August 22, 11am: Jackpot – High Climber: 29mi, 2,400ft- The queen stage. Begin with a few miles of neutral roll along the Gitchi Gami. Chat with fellow racers and take in the view. In Tofte, ascend a tarmac climb to Britton Peak and plug into the singletrack. Pedal, pump, and grit through the Jackpot wilderness. The Gravity Segment here is remote and will test your onsight ability. Keep it rubber side down, help is a long way off out here! Cross onto High Climber at mile 22 and flow through 5 miles of Dirt Candy passing two Gravity Segments along the way, the second one is pure speed! Finish with a jaunt down the Lutsen Mountain Trail and a short punchy two-track to the finish. Save something for this last climb! Post race food, beers, and music at Caribou Highlands near the finish area. 

 

Sunday August 23, 9am: Pincushion Dirt Circuit- 20mi, 2,200ft- The final stage will start and finish in the coolest small town in America. First ascend tarmac, two-track, and a goat trail up to Pincushion. Pedal, pump, and jump around the fully redesigned trail system for two laps (hitting 3 Gravity Segments each lap) and fly back into town. Post race celebration, beer, and awards at Voyageur Brewing in downtown Grand Marais.

San Diego's finest annual cycling event across the Coronado Bridge and around the bay. A fun time for all ages and all skill levels. 

Ride the bridge, Bike the Bay! Cruise around San Diego Bay and enjoy your only opportunity to ride across the San Diego Coronado Bay Bridge. This non-competitive community bike ride is for riders of all abilities and will take you on a scenic, and primarily flat ride, around the San Diego Bay via the Bayshore Bikeway. All riders will return to San Diego for a post-ride festival with food, beverage, beer garden, and entertainment.

The Bike the Bay ride is a fun and non-competitive ride for cyclists of all abilities. We encourage the “go slow and say hello” model. The safety of all riders is our highest priority. Please observe the following rules/restrictions so everyone can enjoy a fun and safe ride:

Helmets are mandatory for all riders

Riders must be over the age of 10 years old to participate

Riders should use bike lanes when available and safe, and ride as close to the right-hand side of the road as practicable.

Riders must obey all rules of the road, traffic signals, crossing signals, and stop signs at all times.

Watch downhill speeds and stay in control at all times.

Unfortunately, due to the significant time and cost of planning this amazing event, we are not able to offer refunds.

Have FUN, be SAFE and ENJOY the ride!

5.You can move up in a Category, but never down.

Go Nuts International Enduro Series eMTB Rules as follows: 

1) Maximum 750watts - assistance up to 20 miles per hour - Pedaling assistance only. No hand or foot throttle allowed. Automatic disqualification. Bicycles must remain locked, i.e., no modification of wheel sensor from factory circumference or any other modification to manipulate the factory set speed of the bike.

2) Throttle mechanisms are prohibited.

3) Studded tires are prohibited.

4) It is forbidden to change e-bike during the event even if the rider finishes the event with the same race plate.

5) Technical assistance consists of the replacement or repairs of any part of the e-bike at the exception of the frame, wheels or battery.

6) Races will be conducted regardless of weather conditions.  In the event of rain or other unfavorable conditions, it may be necessary to alter the order of the event schedule, including but not limited to, adjusting the length of the race or delaying or stopping the program completely.  Should a delay occur, every effort will be made to resume the schedule in a timely fashion if conditions significantly improve.

7) No headphones, earphones or sound devices permitted. Horns and bells are permitted.

8) Riders are required to wear the appropriate helmet. Other protective gear is optional; gloves, goggles, elbow/knee guards, etc.

9) Shirt, shoes, and pants/shorts required. Clipless or flat pedals are both permitted.

10) An E-Mountain Bike is a bike operated with two energy sources, human pedal power and an electric engine, which only provides assistance when the rider is pedaling.

11) Any behavior deemed inappropriate or unsportsmanlike like conduct will not be tolerated. Verbal or physical infractions will result in a disqualification. 

Severe weather policy
Unless otherwise posted, race will be held. Safety of all racers is our main priority. If there is a delay or cancellation due to weather conditions, racers are responsible for checking information posted by director. The information will be posted on the homepage of website, social network avenues, and via email up to 72 hours prior to the race.

Transfer/Refund Policy
There will be no registration refunds once registration is processed. We will allow transfers to upcoming races. All transfers must be requested 10 days prior and is only allowed for races that were rescheduled. Transfers will not be allowed 10 days before race or after race.

EventNotes:
The 50th Brandywine Tour!

Sunday, August 23rd, 2026

 

The Delaware Valley Bicycle Club is pleased to offer our fully supported, highly acclaimed, Brandywine Valley Tour featuring covered bridges, picturesque villages, and amazing vistas! Enjoy any of five gorgeous routes with multiple rest stops serving varied menus including vegan/vegetarian and gluten-free options on request.

 

Our courses are over low-traffic paved roads through the lush, rolling Chester County hills known for its thoroughbred horse farms and beautiful landscapes. Our longer routes venture into the horse and buggy farm areas of Lancaster County. Century riders will roll to a rest stop in the aptly named town of Paradise PA. History buffs will love the historic revolutionary war connection of the nearby Brandywine Battlefield Historic Site. Others will be charmed by beautifully shaded roads winding by the area's many creeks and streams. Just a few miles before your ride's end, cyclists on the 50 and 100-mile routes will roll into one of the region’s best “cow-to-cone” ice cream farms for a refreshing, free ice cream. 

 

Please pay particular attention to the following:

  • All riders are expected to have a fully functional and well-maintained bicycle.
  • Helmets are required.
  • All routes may be navigated with cue sheets (provided) and/or GPS routes.
  • There will be no road marks, but we will place signs at major route splits.
  • Class II electronic bikes (bikes with pedal assist and a throttle) are not permitted on this tour.
  • SAG will be provided until 5 p.m.
  • All routes start at Charles F. Patton Middle School, 760 Unionville Road, Kennett Square PA 19348.

Your tour fees directly benefit the community! Proceeds after tour expenses are distributed to many community organizations. Past donations have included local trails and parks, non-profit cycling organizations and community schools and sports organizations.

 

2025 Road Routes:

  • 20 Miles - A guided ride led by a DVBC ride leader for experienced riders who want a shorter option with approximately 900 feet of climbing and one water/rest break midway along the route.
  • 35 Miles - This route, which climbs about 2000 feet, includes delightful rolls through quaint towns, plus magnificent equestrian farm scenery on the way to and from the Harmony Rest Stop.
  • 50 Miles - Lots of flat stretches but enough hills that you will take notice of about 2971 feet of climbing. This route is so pretty we hope it won't bring tears to your eyes! Two fully stocked rest stops plus lunch at the finish.
  • 66 Miles - Awesome scenery abounds in this ride from Chester County into Lancaster County and back again. Three fully stocked rest stops plus lunch at the finish with a tad under 4000 feet of climbing.
  • 100 Miles – With about 6,000 ft climbing. This town and country ride has it all! We set you off on a moderate and scenic route, then head for the hills and dales of western Chester County and rural Lancaster County. You'll enjoy rolling past gorgeous Octorara Creek. Admire the impossibly tall corn, search for Amish Sunday worshippers with collections of horses and buggies visiting neighborhood farms. Plus you'll find two beautifully restored covered bridges on this route. Four fully stocked rest stops - including a stop in Paradise just for Century riders and a pizza stop - plus lunch at the finish.

Registration Fees:

Sunday Omnium Racing – Northeast Velodrome

Gate opens at 9:30 AM
Racing starts at 10:30 AM

Join us for fast, fun, and welcoming Sunday Omnium racing at the Northeast Velodrome! Whether you’re new to the track or a seasoned racer, we’ve got a field for you and a great environment to race, learn, and progress.

Member Perk

Grassroots Members race for only $10 with your membership discount code.

NEV Members race for free with your membership discount code.

If you’re planning to race more over the season, membership pays for itself quickly.

Race Categories

A Race (Cat 1-3 / Experienced Masters)

B Race (Cat 4/5 / Masters)

A competitive but approachable field for developing racers and masters riders looking for a strong, steady pace.

C / Novice Race (New & C-Level Racers)

New to track racing? This is your place.

  • Gear restriction: 50x15 max
  • Designed to build confidence, skills, and race awareness in a supportive setting

Built-In Coaching for New Riders

We’re committed to developing new racers. The C/Novice field will include rolling coaches riding within the race to:

  • Provide real-time guidance
  • Help with positioning and tactics
  • Ensure a safe, positive first race experience

This is one of the best ways to gain real race experience while learning from experienced riders.

Field Notes & Flexibility

  • Fields may be combined or adjusted based on registration and turnout
  • A Women’s field may be added if there is sufficient interest
  • Race formats may vary slightly to match field size and create the best racing experience for everyone

General Notes

  • Open gearing for A/B categories unless otherwise specified
  • All riders are expected to race safely and respectfully
  • Pre-registration is strongly encouraged—it helps us plan better racing for you

Come out, race hard, learn something new, and be part of a growing track community.

EventNotes:
Irish Hills Gravel Makeup Group Ride

We're excited to invite you to a makeup group ride following the air quality-related cancellation of the Sunday ride during our Gravel Weekend with Paige Onweller.

While we're disappointed that Paige's schedule won't allow her to join us for the rescheduled ride, we're grateful to our friends at the League of Michigan Bicyclists (LMB) for partnering with us to help bring everyone back together for a great day on the bike.

Whether you participated in the original Gravel Weekend or are simply looking for a fun day exploring some of Southern Michigan's best gravel roads, we'd love to have you join us.

New to gravel? Don't worry—we'll have multiple pace groups to make this ride welcoming for riders of a wide range of experience levels.

Ride Details

Date: Sunday, August 23 - 9:00 AM Rollout

Distance: Approximately 44 miles and a 25 Mile option.

We'll ride one of the featured Irish Hills Gravel routes through the scenic gravel roads of the Irish Hills. The course map will be shared with registered participants prior to the ride. 25 Mile riders can will divert courses about 14 miles into the ride.

We'll offer several pace groups so riders can choose the experience that's right for them. The emphasis is on riding together, encouraging one another, and enjoying a great day on the bike—not racing.

What to Bring

  • Your gravel bike (or any bike appropriate for gravel roads)
  • Helmet (required)
  • Water and nutrition
  • Flat repair supplies and basic tools
  • A positive attitude and willingness to have fun!

We look forward to getting everyone back together after Mother Nature had other plans in July. Thanks again for your flexibility, and we'll see you on August 23!

EventName: VTYC Maneuvers Clinic with Meridith McFarland at von Trapp Outdoor Center
EventNotes:
Join us on Tuesday Aug 25th from 9-12 at the von Trapp Outdoor Center for a maneuvers clinic + group ride with Meridith McFarland and coaches from the Bicycle Express Racing Team. 
 
This clinic is geared toward youth in 5th-12th grade who love to play around on bikes and want to improve maneuvers for riding/racing efficiency. We'll practice foundational skills and maneuvers like front/rear wheel lifts, wheelies, track stands, endos, braking and more. 
 
After 1-2 hours of practice in the field, we'll break into groups and ride Trapps trails before heading home.

EventName: The Rift MTB - Iceland Stage Race 2026
EventNotes:
Both team members must meet the minimum age requirement of 18 years old on race day.

The Rift MTB is a five-day stage race for a team of two through the unique landscapes of North Iceland. The routes take you across rugged trails, along the quiet shores of Eyjafjörður fjord, and over highland plateaus with incredible Arctic views. You’ll face steady climbs, fun descents, and stretches of singletrack winding through birch forests and bike parks.

Each day brings something different—gravel roads, remote trails, singletracks and a real sense of adventure. It’s a chance to experience the raw beauty of North Iceland on two wheels.

We are proud to present the Rocky Hill CX Series as a centralized location for our youth teams to practice at (5:00 PM), and a fun, no-pressure, training race for those looking to enjoy cyclocross racing (5:35 PM for the Juniors and 6:15 PM Open Race). This 4-week training series will take place on 4 Wednesdays in August/September. August 26th, Sept 2nd, Sept 9th, and Sept 16th. With respect to the Town of Rocky Hill and their beautiful park, we will cancel due to rain and wet conditions that will be especially damaging to the venue. In this case, we will provide a credit to all participants and you will be notified of a cancelation via email!

This practice is hosted by CCAP staff and regional team coaches. Licensed junior riders under 18 and middle/high schoolers can enjoy a no-pressure practice session at 5:00 PM. Any junior that wants to ride must be at least 9 years old (cyclocross racing age = age on Dec 31st of the 2026 year) and are welcome to race in the Junior Race. All training activities and races will be started with instruction from CCAP coaches and staff. All youth riders, 18 and under, are welcome to participate in the practice for $10. Riders that are on CCAP registered teams may participate in the practice at no charge.

Fun, safe and competitive racing for all
Fun, friendly, and competitive racing for everyone from novice racers to experienced Category 1 Racers. The wide variety of skill levels makes for an informal, no-pressure vibe. 

All riders must have a USA Cycling License. If you don't have one, one-day beginner licenses may be purchased for $15 and are valid for a single day. One-day beginner licenses may only be purchased by new riders or Category 5 riders.

Equipment
All USAC Rules apply. All riders must wear a helmet. A cyclocross bike or mountain bike (without bar-ends) is suggested. No BMX bikes allowed.

Categories.CategoryName: WNYBRC TdT (Tour de Trails or Dead Tulip)

EventNotes:
All rides start and end from Collins Pavilion at Schoen Place (between Aladdin's Natural Eatery & Lock 32 Brewing Company). 
 
There are two route options: The 42-mile “Tour de Trails” loop or the 25-mile “Dead Tulip” loop. All the rides ETA finish times are between 8-9 PM. The “Tour de Trails” route has four staggered start times with varying average speeds:
  • 5:00 PM TdT Ride* (average speed in the range of 11-14 MPH)
  • 5:20 PM TdT Ride* (average speed in the range of 14-16 MPH)
  • 5:40 PM TdT Ride* (average speed in the range of 16-19 MPH)
  • 6:00 PM TdT Ride* (average speed in the range of 19-22 MPH)
  • 6:15 PM Dead Tulip Ride* (average speed in the range of 10-15 MPH)
Please arrive at least 15 minutes early and be ready to roll at the start time. The routes consists of stone dust, gravel, single track, and asphalt surfaces. The routes go on the Erie Canal, Auburn Trail, Domine Trail, Lehigh Trail, Genesee Valley Greenway, Genesee Riverway Trail, Rochester/Syracuse/Eastern Trolley Trail, and the Empire State Trail. 
 
Post ride social banter from 8-10 PM at Collins Pavilion & Lock 32 Brewing Company .  
 
Occasional live music pre/post ride (Check Lock 32 Brewing Events Calendar).
 
Post ride event raffles every week sponsored by N+1 Designs and Bert's Bikes & Fitness. To qualify for raffles you must be registered at www.BikeReg.com/TdT, complete one of the ride routes with one of the groups that day, be a member of WNYBRC Strava Club, and post ride publicly on Strava. Raffle winner will be announced via a BikeReg email for registered participants.

Timing

Use of the timing chips is required if you are participating in the HHH/Wee-Chi-Tah Mountain Bike or Trail run events or the Triple Threat Challenge. The timing chips are disposable so there will be no requirement to return them. The goal is to post early registered rider's times by Sunday evening. Registering for a Community Program at the VPCC for 2026 can include the option of purchasing USA Cycling Membership + Race License. The Membership + Race license benefit is that riders can later compete in competitive events, receive secondary medical insurance, and have the option to purchase on-bike injury coverage with a $0 deductible. Here is the member benefits page: https://usacycling.org/benefits

If you would like to utilize these benefits for your summer camp session, please follow the following process to sign up. 

*If you already have an active USA Cycling Membership +Race License, you can proceed to Step 2, register for your selected summer camp. 

Step 1 — Obtain Your USA Cycling Membership + Race License Number

Proceed to the following web page to get started: https://usacycling.org/get-started-racing Scroll down to the bottom and click on join now to get started.

  • USA Cycling recently adjusted the membership price from $20 to $40. A discount code is available that reduces the membership fee back to $20, regardless of whether auto-renew is selected. This code works for both new and renewing members.  That code is USAC-TW20X.
  • During checkout, riders must open the Discount box near the end of the process to apply the code.
  • The +Race License is free for juniors and free for first-time USA Cycling members for the first year.
  • New members receive a free one-year annual race license, but they must manually add the license to their USA Cycling account.
  • Returning members should review the current USA Cycling fee schedule: https://usacycling.org/schedule-of-fees

If you have a question or need a refund, you must contact USA Cycling Membership directly: https://usacyclinghelp.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/requests/new?ticket_form_id=1900000822164

Step 2 — Register on BikeReg

Once each participant has a valid USA Cycling membership +Race license number, you can continue to or return to BikeReg.com to register for your VPCC program.

We want to ensure all families are aware of how we handle low enrollment and what to expect as we approach the start of camp.

To provide the best experience for participants, level 1 & 2 classes may be combined if registration numbers are low. A class will be combined if a single class has 9 or fewer participants, and if combined classes would still remain under 15 total participants.

If combining classes is needed, the program will shift to the default Monday/Wednesday schedule.

We will make the final determination one week before the start of camp. This allows us to communicate any changes clearly and give families time to plan.

Thank you for your understanding and flexibility as we work to provide a smooth and enjoyable camp experience for all participants. -VPCC Community Programs Manager

Categories and Numbers:  There are three fields for the series:  A, B, and C. You will indicate your field of choice by answering a custom question during registration.

The A field is intended primarily for riders in Category 3 or above.  Category 5 racers should not register for the A field except with prior permission from the race promoter (send email to sunapeeracing@gmail.com), or inquire at the gate during registration.  The B field is recommended for experienced riders with considerable strength.  The C field is recommended for all other riders, including new and slower riders.  If you register for a field and decide you want to make a change before the race, please let us know at the gate.

Junior Membership:  Available to persons 17 years of age or younger.  A parent or guardian will need to be in attendance to sign the waivers for the race and entry into the NHMS facility.  If you are unable to accompany the minor, please make prior arrangements with the race director to ensure that all necessary forms are completed in advance.

NHMS Gate Entry Fee:  The series pass does not include the NHMS gate entry.  The gate entry fee is $10 per adult racer, or $5 for juniors and spectators.  The gate fee is paid directly to NHMS at gate, and helps cover costs of ambulance, personnel and other direct costs associated with hosting the race at their venue. Please Note: Failure to pay the gate fee will result in a permanent ban from participating in the NHMS series. 

Weather Cancellations:  We try hard to avoid cancelling races due to weather, but sometimes mother nature happens.  We will send out cancellation notices by email to all Bikereg registrants.

New Racers:  New racers are always welcome.  If you are a new racer and/or it is your first time at the series, please feel free to contact the race director with any questions or ask for assistance during registration.  The race series is a welcoming environment, and there are many experienced racers at the series who are happy to assist new racers. 

The Courses:  The races are run on four courses:  (1) the road; (2) the inner road; (3) frontier; and (4) the magic mile.  We will attempt to notify racers which course will be used in advance, but do not have control over last minute changes.  For information about the various courses, please see the photographs and information at the bottom of this registration page.

Season Passes:  Season passes are available on bikereg.com: https://www.bikereg.com/nhms

Licenses and Rules:  A USA Cycling license is NOT required for a series pass and/or day-of registration.  All USA Cycling Rules for helmets apply.  No Aero Bars.  Please visit the NHMS page on our website for rules about the series.

The Potential Race Courses:

1.  The Road Course is a 1.5 miles course at NHMS that is used for motorcycle races.  There are two short big ring hills included in this course.  The race length is based on available daylight and will likley be 18 laps (July and August) and 15 laps (September).  Check out Strava for details:  https://www.strava.com/segments/619600

 

2.  The Oval Course is a .9 mile pancake flat course with no elevation gain.  It is typically run with one of the chicanes.  The use of chicanes will be announced at the beginning of the oval race.  Generally a 30 lap race depending on daylight. Length will be announced before the race.  Check out Strava for details:  https://www.strava.com/segments/733975

 

3.  The Frontier Course is a 1 mile course in the back stretch of the NHMS grounds, and includes a moderately technical corner leading into a short incline.  A great course for building power and working on technical skills.  Generally a 24 lap race.  Length will be announced before the race.  Here is the segment on Strava:  http://www.strava.com/segments/619597

4.  The Magic Mile Course was created in 2017 and received rave reviews, and we have now incorporated the Magic Mile course in our rotation.  This is a 1 mile course that races like a fun crit.  Here is the segment on Strava:  https://www.strava.com/segments/15840249

EventName: Indy Cycloplex Short Track Mountain Bike Series 2026
EventNotes:
Indy Cycloplex Short Track Cross Country Mountain Bike Racing 

ICX STXC is a new Short Track Racing Series taking place at the Indy Cycloplex. Aiming to bring MTB racing to the City of Indianapolis, this STXC race series serves as a training/development series for racers to hone their MTB skills. The STXC series will also take place on Marque Race Nights at the Indy Cycloplex, with racing taking place on the Velodrome and BMX track too. Food, Beverages, and Music will be available for all to enjoy during Marquee Race Nights at ICX!

The goal: Provide STXC MTB racing for the greater Indianapolis cycling community.

This series is inclusive of all ability levels and will allow riders to self-select categories independent of USA Cycling categories to provide a chance to race against groups that are similar in skillset and fitness levels. Juniors to Masters, Collegiate and Elite, Men and Women, all are encouraged to race in the wave that presents them the best fit.

Race Day Schedule: (will be the same for all race days)


6:00pm – Junior Men and Women
This is for juniors dipping their toes into STXC racing for
the first time.

These results will be posted at the Indy Cycloplex and on the Indy Cycloplex Website but will not be posted to USA Cycling's website. 

 

6:30pm – Intermediate Men and Women
This is for racers that have some STXC experience and looking for a little challenge. Also for 14–17-year-old juniors that are looking to challenge themselves, Collegiate B’s and C's, and racers that aspire to earn upgrade points for USAC categories

These results will be posted at the Indy Cycloplex and on the Indy Cycloplex Website and will be posted to USA Cycling's website. 

 

7:00pm – Elite Men and Women
This is the fastest field of the evening. Local Pros and the top collegiate riders will race in this category. High level juniors and u23 riders should race in this category, as well as anyone else that is looking for a leg busting challenge on a Thursday night.

These results will be posted at the Indy Cycloplex and on the Indy Cycloplex Website and will be posted to USA Cycling's website. 

 

The course:

Utilizing the infamous Indy Cycloplex “Mountain” (ok, hill!) next to Cold Springs Road, the ICX STXC course will vary from week to week. The starting grid and finish line will be placed in the parking lot of the ICX, and racing will take place on and around the hillside utilizing some of the single-track MTB trails at ICX. Course direction will change from event to event, and different features will be included or removed for each event night as well. All STXC courses will NOT utilize the DS course at ICX, these STXC events are geared toward high intensity single track style MTB racing.

All times EST - Held under USAC permit #10515

• Day-of registration late fee on BikeReg: $10

 

• USA Cycling and Indy Cycloplex waivers required on race day (all riders must check in) 

ICX waiver available online (www.indycycloplex.com/waiver)

Welcome to the Wheeler Rally, a one-of-a-kind endurance gravel event held deep inside the breathtaking Wheeler National Wildlife Refuge on the banks of the Tennessee River. This is your chance to experience what few riders ever do — a fully permitted rally behind the gates of one of Alabama’s most scenic and protected landscapes. The loop is just short of 10 miles.

Choose your challenge:
 3-Hour — perfect for first-timers and those looking to test their gravel legs.
 6-Hour — a solid endurance effort with plenty of time to explore the course.
 9-Hour — the ultimate test of grit, pacing, and heart.

NO RACE DAY REGISTRATION - REGISTRATIN CLOSES 08/27 AT 5:00PM

No matter your distance, you’ll Ride the Refuge — and carry home the memory of one of the most peaceful and awe-inspiring landscapes in the South and and that unmistakable calm that only the Wheeler National Wildlife Refuge can offer. 15% of gross proceeds donated to Friends of Wheeler. The 11th Annual Rose Mountain Rumble (RMR) takes place Saturday, August 29th, 2026. 

Registration opens 7:00 AM, rolling starts begin 7:30 AM.

The RMR is a non-timed gravel ride that tours the scenic dirt roads of Lyndeborough, New Hampshire and surrounding towns. We welcome riders of every ability and offer a variety of route options from a 25-miler for more casual riders, an intermediate 45-miler, to 66 and 80-mile courses that challenge the most competitive gravel grinder.  The RMR is capped at 150 riders.  

All the routes begin and end at Lyndeborough's historic Center Hall.   The 25-mile course is marked, while the 45, 66 and 80-mile courses are not.  Riders need to be prepared to follow provided cue sheets and are strongly encouraged to download the supplied GPX courses ahead of time which can be found at www.rosemountainrumble.com on the Courses page.  

Registration includes water/snack stops, a delicious post-ride lunch provided by the Wilton-Lyndeborough Women’s Club, and a tee-shirt custom-designed each year by local bike builder and graphic artist Kris Henry.  Net proceeds benefit the Piscataquog Land Conservancy, a regional land trust that has been protecting open space in southern New Hampshire since 1970.

We are holding the 2026 registration fee level with last year at $125 per rider.  To help younger riders be part of the Rumble, we are continuing our discounted registration fee for riders 18 and under.  Just contact us and we'll send you a discount code to use at checkout.

We can't wait to see you…get ready to rumble!  - Team RMR

840 N Park Road
Wyomissing, PA

Aaron will email additional information later this week, including the route and important ride details. Please note that this will be a community ride rather than a permitted Barn Gravel event. Sign up for the Go Grava email notification at https://gograva.com/pages/wednesday-night-ride under "Join the Squad". 

They will also be collecting donations that day for Helping Harvest, with the goal of bringing this year's donation to at least $1,000.

What is the future of Barn Gravel?

unPAved Pennsylvania stepped in to help Barn Gravel grow by providing permits, insurance, branding, and a formal structure. While this support helped the event expand, it also unintentionally softened some of the grassroots, social spirit that defined Barn Gravel.

So, we are handing the event back to local leadership, led by Aaron Johnson of GO GRAVA, in hopes that this beloved group ride—which has happened annually for six years—can continue in the spirit in which it began.

Gravel, farm roads, dirt paths, and singletrack… You can ride all that in 1 day right here in Berks county!

Supports Helping Harvest, and we will ask every participant to bring a food item or cash donation during registration to support local hunger efforts and farmers.

EventName: AES | Round 1 | Bentonville - Bella Vista Enduro
EventNotes:
BENTONVILLE + BELLA VISAT ENDURO | AUGUST 29-30, 2026

The Bentonville - Bella Vista Enduro highlights the best of Northwest Arkansas, where an extensive network with hundreds of miles of world-class trails and multiple trail systems creates a proper canvas for an epic day of enduro racing in the Mountain Biking Capital of the World™.

Registration opens Friday, June 12th at 8am with participation based on a first-come, first-served basis. To create a rewarding enduro race experience, organizers reserve the right to limit overall event participation. Each participant’s entry includes:

  • One-day competition with up to 4-7 stages and 10-20 total miles of rider-designed racing with dedicated pre-race practice times the day prior to the race.
  • Sufficiently marked courses with maps emailed to participants the week of the event.
  • Lively mid-race aid stations with access to professional neutral mechanics and medical support.
  • Professional event timing with accuracy to the 1000th of a second and instant results.
  • Complimentary post-race meal and cold beverages (21+ for adult beverages, ID required) in a family-friendly festival setting.
  • Awards ceremony by category with prizes awarded 5 deep.

RACE VENUE

The Bentonville - Bella Vista Enduro will start in Bella Vista near the Allen's Food Market. 

Race Venue Address - 60 Sugar Creek Center, Bella Vista, AR 72714

 

EVENT SCHEDULE

Final event schedule with packet pickup, official pre-ride, and start times will be released the week of the event. Arkansas Enduro Series events are rain or shine except under extreme circumstances. When permittable, an official pre-ride/practice will be scheduled the day prior to Race Day(s). The Race Director reserves the right to adjust the schedule due to any unforeseen circumstances.

FRIDAY |

  • Early pre-riding is allowed although some stages may in the proccess of being finishing marking.
  • 4PM-7PM | Early Check-In | Location TBA

SATURDAY |

  • 9AM-4PM | Check-In & Official Practice Day

SUNDAY | 

  • 8AM-10AM | Timing Chip Pick-Up according to Wave Times. Late Check-In available.
  • 9AM-3PM | Race Day
  • 4PM | Podium Awards

Arkansas Enduro Series events are rain or shine except under extreme circumstances. When possible, an official practice will be scheduled the day prior to Race Day(s). The Race Director reserves the right to adjust the schedule due to any unforeseen circumstances. 

 

SAFETY - This is not the time to skimp on protective equipment. Helmets are required to be worn on course during official event times and we highly suggest a full-face helmet, knee pads, and elbow pads.

TEMPERATURE - In August, Bella Vista experiences hot and humid summer weather. Average daily highs range from 87°F to 89°F, while overnight lows drop into the mid-to-upper 60s (around 65°F to 69°F)

WATER & SNACKS - While hydration will be available at select locations on course, riders are encouraged to plan to carry at least 50-60 ounces of water and enough snacks to sustain themselves under strenuous exercise.

NICE TO HAVES - Bug spray, sunscreen, spare tubes, pump or CO2, plugs, patches and other parts.

DOGS - Dogs are allowed but are required to be on a leash at all times. No exceptions.

TRASH - If you pack it in, pack it out. We are guests. Please follow all event sustainability and recycling requests.

RACE DAY MEAL - A post-race meal will be provided to racers and volunteers on Race Days only. Redeemable meal tickets will be provided at the Registration & Timing tent. When possible, additional food trucks and other resources will be made available on-site for fans, family and friends.

WAIVER - All participants will be required to sign a waiver of liability prior to competing in the Arkansas Enduro Series.

REFUND POLICY - Arkansas Enduro Series events are rain or shine, and refunds will not be issued except under extreme circumstances. The Event Organizer reserves the right to adjust the schedule due to any unforeseen circumstances including rescheduling the event to a future date.

If participants choose to add additional Registration Protector through BikeReg, those claims are handled entirely by Allianz Global Assistance. For policy questions or to file a claim visit www.eventregistrationprotection.com or call 1-888-799-2832.

SERIES RULES - additional series information and rules available at www.arkansasenduroseries.com/rules.

NVP continues its tradition of offering a variety of scenic rides through quiet back roads in Massachusetts and (for the 100 mile ride) New Hampshire. EventName: Corsa Coppi Criterium -- Event #8 in the 2026 MABRA Road Series
EventNotes:
WELCOME!   Squadra Coppi is excited to welcome racers, families, friends, and spectators to the inaugural Corsa Coppi Criterium at Chinquapin Park in Alexandria, VA. Located in the heart of Alexandria, the event features a fast and technical loop course, closed to vehicle traffic, that is suitable for riders of all categories. We look forward to hosting a competitive and enjoyable day of racing while showcasing one of Alexandria's premier recreational destinations.

THE COURSE:  The race will be contested on a 0.5-mile closed-loop course utilizing Chinquapin Dr. around Chinquapin Park. The course features smooth pavement, multiple turns, and excellent spectator viewing opportunities. Riders should familiarize themselves with the course prior to racing and are encouraged to participate in any scheduled course preview sessions.

COURSE ADDRESS:

Chinquapin Park
3210 King Street
Alexandria, VA 22302

DIRECTIONS:  Chinquapin Park is conveniently located in Alexandria, Virginia, just minutes from Interstate 395, Duke Street, and Old Town Alexandria. Participants are encouraged to use Google Maps navigation to the event address listed above.

PARKING:  Parking will be available at the First Baptist Church of Alexandria:

First Baptist Church of Alexandria
2932 King Street
Alexandria, VA 22302

Please respect all parking instructions, posted signage, and volunteer direction. Our ability to continue using these facilities depends on participants parking only in approved areas and leaving the facilities clean and undamaged.

LICENSING: USAC Road rules apply.  A racing license is required to enter; please provide your USAC license # when registering online, and be prepared to show your license at check-in.  Unlicensed riders may race only in categories that are open to Novice (Cat. 5) riders, and will be charged an additional $15 in their BikeReg shopping cart for a 1-Day license.

ENTRY FEES:  The entry fee for Juniors (Racing Age 9-18) is $20.00 for all races they are eligible to enter.  The entry fee for all other riders is $50.00 for the first race and $25.00 for additional races.  Note that the multi-entry discount is applied automatically only when the entries are purchased in the same BikeReg shopping cart; otherwise use the 'Contact Us' link below to request a partial refund for the second race.  For second entries purchased on race day, inquire at the day-of registration table for a coupon code to receive the discount at checkout.  BikeReg assesses a service charge for each entry purchased.  A surcharge of $10.00 will be assessed for adult riders purchasing their first entry on race day; for Junior riders the surcharge will be $5.00.  Entry fees are non-refundable.

RACE DAY REGISTRATION & CHECK-IN:  Race-day registration and rider check-in will be located near the start/finish area. Riders must check in and collect their race numbers prior to competing. Check-in will open at least 1 hour prior to the start of the first scheduled race and will close 20 minutes prior to the scheduled start time of each race.

Please arrive early to allow sufficient time for parking, check-in, number pickup, and course familiarization.

Entry fees will be collected only through BikeReg.  There will be no in-person sales at the event.  Riders who pre-register by the Thursday 8:30 AM closing of pre-registration will have pre-assigned bibs, and will receive email notification of their bib numbers prior to race day; riders who register after the page re-opens will be assigned bibs at the event.  If you are pre-registered, please memorize your bib number; if you have a USA Cycling Annual license, please pull the license up on your phone before you get in line to check in.  

PRO TIP #1:  don't wait until you go to register (or worse, until race day) to renew your USAC racing license, as it can take a couple of days for the renewal to propagate through the USAC system before BikeReg (and we!) can see it.

PRO TIP #2:  hands-down, the best way to always have your USAC racing license on-hand is to add it to your Google or Apple wallet.  Login to your USAC account to get started.

If you miss the closing of pre-registration, you must complete the registration process on BikeReg when the page re-opens, then wait to receive your confirmation email before getting in line to check in at the event.  Present your confirmation, along with your USA Cycling racing license (or if you are racing on a 1-Day license, your BikeReg receipt), and we will issue your bib.  Registration will be open for each category until 20 minutes prior to the scheduled start of the race.  Don't be “that guy/gal” – plan ahead and arrive timely!

START TIMES:  All race start times are estimates and may be adjusted based on race-day conditions, field sizes, or unforeseen circumstances. Participants should listen for announcements and remain near the staging area prior to their scheduled events.

WEATHER:  The event will be held rain or shine. Race officials reserve the right to modify, shorten, delay, or cancel races if conditions are determined to be unsafe.

COMBINED CATEGORY RACES will race together as one field, and will be uploaded to USA Cycling and road-results as a single field, but will be scored separately for podiums and prize lists.  The Junior fields will start separately by 2 age groups, and will be scored separately.  The Masters 45+ field will start 1 minute ahead of the Masters 55+/65+ field, and each age group will be scored separately for podiums and prize lists.

SPECTATORS:  Spectators are encouraged to attend and enjoy the racing from designated viewing areas around the course. Please remain clear of the race roadway and follow all instructions from race officials and volunteers.

COMMUNITY PARTNERS:  We would like to thank Alexandria City High School, First Baptist Church of Alexandria, the City of Alexandria, our volunteers, sponsors and local cycling community for helping make this event possible.

QUESTIONS:  for registration or eligibility inquiries, contact SpacemanEventServices@gmail.com; for general race inquiries, contact squadracoppibod@googlegroups.com.

WHAT: kids' mountain bike race followed by a free trailhead cookout

Race categories span from pre-K to 12th grade and the race course changes with each age range.

EventName: The Ride Series MTB Skills Clinics: JUMP BASICS Sat 8-11 & JUMP PROGRESSION Sun 8-11
EventNotes:
The Ride Series is different. Your expectations should be high as you enter the hospitality of our classroom setting. A comfortable Kijaro chair awaits your presence and the cover our 10x20 tents provides reprieve from the elements. Prepare yourself to be immersed in an environment that provides the perfect opportunity for you to be open to embracing and practicing the proper technique. Instant feedback from our coaching staff will have you progressing like never before! Are YOU ready??

JUMP ESSENTIALS: 

We get it, everyone wants to jump! However, most people don't embrace the technique AND psychology behind doing it well. You have to understand the what and why before you can start to build confidence with the how, that's what this session is for. Not only will you build a solid understanding of what NEEDS to happen, you'll also get plenty of reps working through the steps of how it needs to happen, all in a safe and controlled environment. 

Topics Covered: 

Riders will get plenty of reps on multiple takeoffs/landings and Rich will work through multiple rounds of video so you can see exactly what's working and what isn't. 

JUMP PROGRESSION Session: Ground School and All American Hero's Jumpline

This event is all about getting comfortable in the air. That starts with a solid understanding of what it takes to get into the air properly. It's also critical to get as MANY reps as possible in a controlled environment and that's what the TRS ground school setting gives you.

Rich will break down the dynamics involved with jumping a bike. Based on over 40 years of experience, he will guide you through his real world experience and provide key insight and cues on what to do. 

After showcasing the proper technique, you'll work through a series of reps and the distance will incrementally increase as your comfort level increases. Analysis and feedback using slow motion video will have you "busting big" in no time.

There's no substitute for experience when it comes to jumping a bike. The only problem is that experience in the right setting can be hard to come by. You'll get tons reps on our jump lines and receive valuable feedback in the moment.
RIDERS MUST HAVE:
- Experience jumping
- Full suspension bikes with suspension in working order
- Full safety gear including pads (Full Face helmet not required, but suggested)

This class is intended for riders with jump experience and will move at a specified pace. Coaching staff reserves the right to hold riders to pre determined distances based on performance.

Please reach out if you are unsure if this class is a proper fit for you.

Cranky Monkey Mountain Bike Race

The Cranky Monkey heads to Rosaryville State Park in 2026!  Join us for an awesome day of bike racing and community.

Race day information sent to riders

Race Date: Sunday August 30, 2026 (rain date 9/27)

Volunteer sign-up

Race Courses: 4 XC courses varying in length from about 6 miles miles to over 30 miles.  See course notes below for course information and maps.

  • Beginner – 5.6ish miles
  • Base –  9ish miles
  • Sport – 20ish miles
  • Expert – 30ish miles

Rosaryville State Park in Upper Marlboro, MD is an absolute gem and one of the most beginner friendly and fun parks in our area for mountain biking. We’ve been hosting races at Rosaryville for over 15 years and are excited to bring back the Cranky Monkey to this very special park. We’ve designed four courses for this race – beginner, base, sport, and expert. They are each described below. All courses start and end at the day use pavilions near the power lines that traverse the park. The start of the race is designed to allow for an exciting, but not overly crowded race start.

  • Beginner (~5.6 miles) – the beginner course is just shy of 6 miles long with about 400 feet of elevation change. It is designed to provide a safe and achievable entrance to mountain bike racing for participants of a variety of ages. The course highlights the western portion of the Perimeter Trail, which is the main multi-use trail in the park.
  • Base (~9 miles) – the base course is a step up fro the beginner course both in length and difficulty. It is about 9 miles in length with 600 feet of elevation change. The base course also highlights the western portion of the Perimeter Trail and also adds in the more technical Tilly Trail.
  • Sport (~20 miles) – the sport course provides a grand tour of the Rosaryville trail system and comes in at about 20 miles in length with about 1,500 feet of elevation change. The sport course highlights the entire Perimeter and Tilly Trails plus a bit.
  • Expert (~30 miles) – the expert course provides a grand route of the Rosaryville trail system and comes in about about 30 miles in length with about 2,200 feet of elevation change. The expert course highlights two complete loops of the Perimeter and Tilly Trails plus a bit.

All the trails at Rosaryville are largely maintained by volunteers organized by the Mid-Atlantic Off-Road Enthusiasts (MORE).  All racers will have the opportunity to donate to the Rosaryville Trail Fund during registration.

EventName: Bike Hub Sunday Epic V5 - Grass Mtn Sufferfest
EventNotes:
The Bike Hub is proud to announce our Sunday Epic ride series! These are all-day rides featuring some of the best mixed-terrain riding the tri-state area has to offer. Forgotten woods roads, fast gravel, rugged singletrack, and even a bit of hike-a-bike. These rides will be long, difficult, and absolutely beautiful. While there is no perfect bike for a Sunday Epic, anything with around a 2 inch tire will work. More details on terrain will be included in each event post. Sunday Epic's will be held the third Sunday of every month from April-September. Start location may vary, but will usually end will some sort of food and drink situation. Wheels down at 8am always.

 This one is gonna be extra tough. Bring a mountain bike of some sort, curly bars may not get you far. My goal here was to put together a ride with the toughest possible terrain and most amount of climbing in the least mileage. Enter the Grass Mtn Sufferset. If you've never visited this area you are in for a treat. Starts and ends at the Shaftsbury Historical Society on 7A, park by the red barn.

 

A few notes on the nitty-gritty of these rides. 

  • Sunday Epic's are fully self supported. Bring everything you need to successfully finish the route. We expect you to carry basics like spare tube, pump, multi-tool, patch kit, food and water, etc. Although we occasionally stop at a convenience store, there are many times where the ride is too remote for that to be an option.
  • We generally try to ride together, but you are welcome to do your own thing as long as you have the route. Group pace usually hovers somewhere around the 10mph average mark, but may be slower depending on terrain/climbing.
  • Expect this to take a good chunk of the day. Occasional stops for snacks etc. We move pretty continuously, but also aren't in a rush. 

RideWithGPS link here.

Note that we don't charge anything for these rides, but we do welcome donations! We are a community-based 501c3 nonprofit focused on removing barriers to cycling for all within the tri-state area. We provide education, free access to bikes and cycling accessories, and provide a place for people of all ages and abilities to connect through cycling. Please read this!
 

Welcome to our FREE monthly ride! Ride start times vary by season to give us the best trail conditions and safest experience—May through September we roll out at 9:00 AM CT, and October through April we begin at 2:00 PM CT. We meet at the lower parking lot at Turkey Mountain Urban Wilderness Park, 6800 S Elwood Ave, Tulsa, OK 74132. Restrooms are available.

 

We will have ride leaders for skill levels between Beginner to Advanced. If you're new to mountain biking, OR have never taken WeROK’s Fundamentals, or other formal fundamentals skills clinics (even if you have been riding some), we REQUIRE YOU to start with the WeROK Fundamental Skills Session during registration. Regardless of your riding experience we feel taking this skills session will help improve your riding and create a better riding experience for all.

 

Loaner Bikes: Please refer to your registration confirmation letter. 
 

Cancellation/Bad Weather Policy: If bad weather develops we aim to cancel the event by 7:00 am the day of the ride.  Stay tuned to social media for announcements. We also follow Trailbot, in case Turkey Mountain trails are “closed” or “delayed”.  We do not have “rain dates”. 

 

Choosing appropriate group: First choose your riding and fitness level, then choose the best description among the groups. Once a group fills, the waitlist option will open. If you have a friend with the same skill level with whom you want to ride, help us out by registering together ASAP, in the same ride level, AND in same group number. Other than cancellations, we CANNOT GUARANTEE we can make any changes to groups, especially at the last minute, since we have group size restrictions. This delivers the best possible ride experience for all! If you don't end up riding with your friends, don't worry, you'll have the opportunity to make new ones!
 

Not sure which group to join? Ride levels are based on YOUR CURRENT skill and endurance levels. We want everyone to have the best and safest experience possible so we use a “rating” system to help align you with the right ride group. Please review the skills, endurance, mileage and proposed trails. Being in the right group makes a better, safer ride for all. If you are still unsure about which group might be for you just contact us at ride@werok.org. P.S. It is perfectly fine to “repeat” a level! Mastery of ALL levels takes time and practice. Please don’t rush yourself, nor succumb to peer pressure. NOTE: WeROK’s skill level names and colors are relative to Turkey Mountain trails. Other trail systems’ color designations could mean their Blue is (y)our Black, so be wise!
 

Advancing to next groups: A great way to know if you are ready to progress to the next ride level is if (1) you felt comfortable with skills necessary at your current level, and (2) you were able to keep up with the ride leader the entire ride and felt like you could have ridden longer. 

 

GROUP CHOICES:
 

1. FUNDAMENTAL SKILLS SESSION 

Select this group if you have never ridden a mountain bike, it’s been longer than you’d like to admit, OR you've never taken any type of basic mtb skills lessons before. Welcome! You have to start somewhere and this is the place! Even the most advanced riders should brush up on these essentials, and certainly, if you feel rusty, this session will help you. This session will cover the fundamentals of mountain biking, and then you'll hit the trail for a 2-3 mile ride. Successful completion of WeROK’s Fundamentals (or its equivalent) is required for advancement to next groups. Departure from this policy requires approval by a WeROK ride leader.

  • Skill Level: Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals are required (we may have loaner pedals available; email us ahead of time at ride@werok.org).
  • Skills you can perform: no requirement, you will definitely learn a skill or two after this session. 
  • Fitness Level: No requirement other than participate in possible heat for up to 2 hours.
  • Example of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, no rocks; double track near Bomb Cellar; the grassy fields; the Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop. 

2. FUNDAMENTALS TO GREEN Group

Select this group if you have taken the Fundamental Skills session, you feel more confident with those skills, and you are looking for a very easy-going transition to green trails. You will have a skills refresher for up to 15 minutes.

  • Skill Level: Confident Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals strongly encouraged (see above re: loaner pedals).
  • Skills you can perform: Staying upright while pedaling, skills learned in Fundamentals Group are beginning to make sense, and your confidence is growing.
  • Fitness Level: Completed a Fundamentals session with minimal fatigue
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with occasional flat, mellow rocks or roots, no significant downhill or uphill; Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop; the very first section of LoChi Connector.
  • Duration: 3-5 miles, maybe longer in cooler weather, no longer than 1.5 hours after refresher portion

3. GREEN Group
You’ve ridden on the dirt trails multiple times by now, and you’re getting the hang of things. You’re mastering the Fundamentals Skills, and your bike operating and handling skills feel smoother. No Fundamentals refresher portion provided.

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: Level pedals while coasting; one finger braking; becoming more comfortable with neutral and ready positions; and smoother corners/berms.
  • Fitness level: Able to ride steady at a comfortable pace for 30 minutes on easy terrain, and may need a breather while climbing, or at the top.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with a variety of low, smooth surface changes; more variety of up and downhill; LoChi; UHF or All Up with rests.
  • Duration: 5-7 miles,1.5 to 2.0 hours 

4. OPEN Group

Looking for new challenges! You are ready to explore more trail features (obstacles) and a variety of up and downhills, with limited stops. Mileage varies. No Fundamentals refresher provided. 

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus-to-Intermediate.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: GREEN skills are solid, but you’re out of saddle more instinctively with level pedals; in and out of neutral/ready position more smoothly; frequent appropriate shifting; smoother, smoother berms and corners; want to ride across straight bridges and skinnies 3-5 feet wide; comfortable choosing lines through rockier terrain, or between tight trees.
  • Fitness level: You’re riding a few times a week. Can ride a WeROK course continuously unless learning steep or more technical terrain. Pushing the pace uphill.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, more roots and rocks, twists and turns. The small bridge on OLD Lo Chi, All Up, UHF, Stay Gold Loop, Naharkey clockwise, maybe counterclockwise. Sessioning features within your skill set, such as the small skinny on Family Loop.
  • Duration: 8-10 miles, 2 hours with some stopping.

About DRRT:

Dirt Rock n Root Training's owner Kathi Krause has been around the bike block – from velodrome and road racing to cyclocross, XC and finally her true love: downhill. She spent a decade on the Pro downhill circuit, stacking up three Masters World DH Championships, five national titles and a win at the legendary Kamikaze Downhill.

After 25 years of racing, Kathi shifted gears to coaching and founded Dirt Rock n Root Training in 2011 . Since then, she's been helping riders find their flow on everything from lift-accessed bike parks to rocky, rooty singletrack. You'll find her leading her Technical Trail series of clinics in North Jersey or running women's clinics at Mountain Creek Bike Park.  Her mission? Simple:  Get more women and kids on bikes, help them crush fear and build a community that rides hard and supports harder.

When not coaching, you can find Kathi out doing what she loves most - shredding the rocks and roots of NJ or dropping into her home trails at Mountain Creek Bike Park.

EventNotes:
Women's Cyclocross Skills Clinic — Northeast Ohio Cyclocross

Sunday, August 30th | 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM 

Location: Cumberland Park, 1740 Cumberland Rd, Cleveland Hts, OH 44118

Whether you're brand new to 'cross or looking to sharpen your handling before race day, this clinic is your chance to build confidence on the bike in a fun, low-pressure setting. All levels are welcome — this is the most accessible discipline in cycling, and there's no better way to try it out or level up your skills.

We're building a mini-course covering every core cyclocross skill: mounts and dismounts, barriers, cornering, carries, cambers, and starts. You'll work through each skill station with course breakdown, bike handling tips, and hands-on coach feedback along the way.

This clinic will be held rain or shine — both are part of racing 'cross, so come dressed for the weather and ready to ride. We do have a pavilion to take breaks and keep gear dry!

Parking: Pool parking area next to the basketball courts. Our pavilion is behind the pool area. 

Cost: Free 

Bikes: Any bike works — cyclocross, gravel, or mountain bike in good repair are all welcome. We will have Jerry Shere available to help with any mechanical issues that arise during the clinic

RSVP: [www.bikereg.com/neocx-clinic  contact korinevanscoach@gmail.com or toveshere@gmail.com  ] 

Your Coaches

Tove Shere

Tove holds a BA in Physical Education and has worked as a personal trainer, strength and conditioning coach, and USA Triathlon coach since 1995. A 7x National Champion in Cyclocross as a Masters athlete, she also earned a silver medal at the 2008 Cyclocross Masters World Championships in Belgium. Beyond 'cross, Tove has competed across a wide range of disciplines — time trials, duathlon, triathlon, snowshoe, and cross country skiing — bringing decades of multi-sport experience to her coaching. 

 

 

Korin Evans 

Korin is the founder of Whole Body Athlete, a strength and nutrition coaching business for active women and endurance athletes. She's a certified personal trainer, nutrition coach and menopause coaching specialist who has worked in health and fitness since 2019. She's competed in many cycling disciplines including; road racing, criteriums, mountain bike and gravel, but cyclocross is her most favorite. She was the Ohio State Masters Champion in Cyclocross in 2022, finisher at Crushar in the Tushar Gravel, Beaver, Utah in 2019 and has been racing competitively for 13 years.

Schedule

10:00 AM – 2:00 PM: Skills Clinic 

Rotating stations covering mounts/dismounts, barriers, cornering, carries, cambers, and starts, with coach instruction and feedback throughout. 

We’ll start with a course walk, move through each station, learn ‘course breakdown’ then run practice laps at the end.

What to Bring

  • Any off-road bike in good working condition (cyclocross, gravel or mountain bike)

  • Helmet is REQUIRED
  • Water Bottle
  • Snacks, water and electrolytes will be provided by Whole Body Athlete Coaching

  • Weather-appropriate clothing — this clinic runs rain or shine — we have a pavilion to keep gear dry in wet weather!

It's a race against the clock! The Calaveras Time Trial by Team Fremont is a great race for everyone of all different skill levels on the beautiful Calaveras Road in Sunol, CA. Whether you are a seasoned road racer, triathlete, a junior racer or a beginner, we have a category for you.

REGISTRATION: Online Registration ONLY. Closes midnight, Thursday August 27. 2026. Entry are fees $50 except Juniors Cat $20, fees include $3 NCNCA and $5.99 USAC insurance surcharges. The Calaveras TT is part of the NCNCA BAR/BAT, NCNCA Juniors Series & the 2025 NCNCA Junior District TT Championship.

DIRECTIONS: From I-680, take the Highway 84 exit and go north on Paloma Road (84) to Sunol. Bear left on 84 onto Niles Canyon road and then turn right on to Main Street to Sunol Glen School. Follow signs to parking. From Niles Canyon (Fremont), exit at Sunol turn right on Main Street. Follow signs to parking.

COURSE: 10 miles on excellent to fair pavement, this is an out and back course. One major climb of 350 feet going to the turn. Start and finish are located approx. 300 yards South of I-680 on Calaveras Road. Turn at the 5.0 miles mark, 1 mile up the hill and past Geary road and retrace. Juniors 9-10 will have a 5 mile course.

WARM UP: Trainer or rollers. No warming up on course.

RULES: USAC Permit 202X-XXXX. A 2026 USAC license required, or purchase a 1-day license during pre-registration or on Bike Reg. No time trial bikes are allowed for all Junior Categories, see USAC Rule 1I5 pg. 31. All USA Cycling rules and code of conduct will be enforced. Juniors 15-18 up may use Time Trial Bikes in non-junior categories. MERCKX: no aero bars or clip-ons, no TT helmet (or face shield), and no wheels deeper than 60mm (paying homage to how Merckx set the hour record in 1972). All other categories may use Time Trial Bikes (except U14).

Start times will be posted at OnTheDay.net 

We'll email you a link to the start lists on August 28th. First rider will depart the start at 8:01 and following riders will depart in the above category order at 60 second intervals. Field limited to 360 total start slots due to parking constraints.

SECOND RIDES: There will be a break after the Junior categories to enable as many 2nd rides as possible. Race Merckx or Masters before the break and your category after the break.

2026 NCNCA Junior District Championship is as follows: The riders must hold an annual license: riders from outside the NCNCA District are welcomed to compete, the title/jersey will be awarded to an annual license holder residing in the NCNCA Region. Juniors in the 9-10 year old category is part of the non-championship category and will ride a 5 mile course.

USAC 7J3 Eligiblity: (a) to be eligible for a State Championship jersey or medal, a rider must hold a current USA Cycling annual license and reside in the state as shown as the rider’s license. (b) State championships are open to US Citizens and permanent residents (green card) with a USA Cycling annual license. (c) Members of UCI Road teams are not eligible for road championships unless there is a separate class for them. (d) at the option of the Administrators, State Championships may include rider who are ineligible for the championship but championships will be awarded to only riders who are eligible.

Member Pricing

Categories.CategoryName: Training Race for CCAP Coaches and Volunteers

EventNotes:
Day of Registration will be available. Adults are $40 & Juniors are $25.

Day of registration spots are limited to the remaining spaces in each field. We cannot guarantee that you will be able to race.

We are proud to present the Rocky Hill CX Series as a centralized location for our youth teams to practice at (5:00 PM), and a fun, no-pressure, training race for those looking to enjoy cyclocross racing (5:35 PM for the Juniors and 6:15 PM Open Race). Thanks to the Town of Rocky Hill Parks and Rec and our partner clubs for allowing this to happen!

Volunteers are needed to make this event successful. Sign up to volunteer and you will receive reimbursement on your entry fee. CLICK HERE TO HELP OUT

Series Dates:
This 4-week training series will take place on 4 Wednesdays in August/September. August 26th, Sept 2nd, Sept 9th, and Sept 16th. With respect to the Town of Rocky Hill and their beautiful park, we will cancel due to rain and wet conditions that will be especially damaging to the venue. In this case, we will provide a credit to all participants and you will be notified of a cancelation via email!

A fun, safe and positive weekly Junior Practice Session
This practice is hosted by CCAP staff and regional team coaches. Licensed junior riders under 18 and middle/high schoolers can enjoy a no-pressure practice session at 5:00 PM. Any junior that wants to ride must be at least 9 years old (cyclocross racing age = age on Dec 31st of the 2026 year) and are welcome to race in the Junior Race. All training activities and races will be started with instruction from CCAP coaches and staff. All youth riders, 18 and under, are welcome to participate in the practice for $10. Riders that are on CCAP registered teams may participate in the practice at no charge.

Fun, safe and competitive racing for all
Fun, friendly, and competitive racing for everyone from novice racers to experienced Category 1 Racers. The wide variety of skill levels makes for an informal, no-pressure vibe. 

All riders must have a USA Cycling License. If you don't have one, one-day beginner licenses may be purchased for $15 and are valid for a single day. One-day beginner licenses may only be purchased by new riders or Category 5 riders.

Equipment
All USAC Rules apply. All riders must wear a helmet. A cyclocross bike or mountain bike (without bar-ends) is suggested. No BMX bikes allowed.

New to cyclocross?
Check out THIS VIDEO to learn what it's all about!

For full information about our weekly race series, we encourage you to visit our website: https://catamountoutdoor.org/race-series-weekly/

 

In the event that the race is cancelled for inclement weather, your entry can be transferred to a different week.

 

A huge thank you to our 2026 series sponsors! 

Gold Level

Central Vermont Runners, MoveWell, SDR Clothing Company

The CXTT is a series of practice races. Cyclists race against the clock on a 2-3 mile course in Kingswood Park in Deerfield Township. This gives the everyone an opportunity to reconnect with the cyclocross community, tune their equipment and training, and give folks new to the sport to try it out in a no-pressure environment.

The CXTT will be on Wednesdays, August 12, 19, 26, and September 2. Riders are called to line up around 6:15, with the first rider starting at 6:30.

Single week registration is $15/rider. Registration and signed waiver is due on noon on race day. You will receive a race number which you will need for the whole series

World famous Wednesday Worlds cyclocross practice at Holster Park, in Clifton NJ. Come build skills and fitness for the cyclocross racing season. 

Wheels down 5:30 - we will do a mix of skills and drills to build fitness before moving on to hot lap and race pace efforts. Session ends around 730 depending on weather, daylight and conditions.  Meet at the tennis courts.  

Location:  https://www.google.com/maps/place/Holster+Park/@40.8593319,-74.188589,16z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x89c2ffb3b0eb8ab1:0xa15abc2860c1a7ec!8m2!3d40.8593319!4d-74.1860141!16s%2Fg%2F1tdwr0j4?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI0MDgyOC4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D

Important info:

  • This is a training group, not a race. Beginners are encouraged and very welcome, but be please be aware that cyclocross is physically demanding and requires a fair level of fitness.   
  • We ride in a public park and conditions may change each week. We are guests in the park and will do everything to keep it clean and respect the rules.
  • We respect others in the park. We respect each other. No fighting. All are welcome.  
  • Helmet is required. Bring a cyclocross (or MTB) bike in good working order.
  • Park on the road between the school and the baseball field. Do NOT park in the fenced area behind the school.  
  • Event may be cancelled due to weather.  Check your email and join the Facebook Group for the latest info.
  • Be nice to each other.
